To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the splitting failure of a moment-resisting doweling joint can be predicted by a quasi-non-linear fracture-mechanics approach; and (2) a simple design approximation is proposed, and its predictions are compared with test data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the splitting failure of dowel joints.
the splitting failure of dowel-type joints in moment resisting connections of steel beams and concrete slabs.
a quasi-non-linear fracture mechanical approach for splitting failure of moment resisting dowel joints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quasi-non-linear model provides a very good approximation for the splitting failure in moment-resistant dowel-type joints.
the model predictions are in reasonable agreement with the test results.
dowel-type connections can provide an effective moment resistance, but the dowels must be located sufficiently far from the beam end to ensure that the splitting failure mode is avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model is capable of predicting the influence of the end distance, the edge distance, and the dowel diameter.
the quasi-non-linear fracture mechanical analysis can predict the splitting strength of moment-resisting joints very well.
the proposed model provides good predictions of the influence on the joint strength of the edge and end distances, and it is also suitable for practical design purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
splitting failure of a dowel joint can be avoided by keeping the dowel away from the beam end and/or by increasing the edge distance.
the proposed model is able to capture the influence of end and edge distances and that a simple approximation of the model is suitable for practical design.
the quasi-non-linear fracture model can be successfully used to predict the splitting failure in dowel-type fasteners.
